We've covered several reports on the use of Apple Vision Pro in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgical procedure using an innovative app on Vision Pro.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, performed using the SportSuite Vision app, which brings "critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space," including arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT imaging.

Below is Stryker's description of the app:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to see both physical objects and digital tools simultaneously in the operating room, such as arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT imaging. When performing arthroscopic surgery, surgeons typically need to rely on multiple displays in the operating room to view imaging and surgical data. By consolidating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional displays and support a more streamlined, ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. According to Stryker, this is the first mobile app authorized by the FDA for intraoperative use on Vision Pro.

Also this week, Pfizer announced it is using Apple Vision Pro to "create a memorable immersive experience" to "showcase" its commitment to "conquering cancer."

You can learn more about the experience on the Groove Jones website.
